title: quant-interop-corridor-weekly-log-mar28-2028
body:
Snapshot notes from the weekly Applied-ML research sync (quant + evals + onboarding). This is a working log — rough, includes open questions and immediate next steps. Aim: capture where we are on heterogeneous quant profiles, eval regressions, and onboarding checklist friction.

1) Quick TL;DR
- Microbatch + KV-prefetch experiment shows 8–12% throughput improvement on p3dn for 8k seq when using hybrid 4/8-bit kernels, but a small perplexity delta on some prompts (~0.6–1.2 ppl).
- Two eval suites flagged a regression on code-completion style prompts when using symmetric 4-bit quant (ML-7823). Root cause suspect: layernorm activation scaling interacting with int4 pack ordering.
- Onboarding checklist: model A (community-11B-compact) now passes latency SLO in dedicated pool but still fails per-token cost target due to batching inefficiencies. Need batching config tweaks.

2) Standup captures (3/28)
- Aisha: ran larger microbatch sweep (batch sizes 1..8, kv-prefetch on/off). Saved traces and flame graphs in GH artifact. Noticed KV miss rate drops ~18% with prefetch for conversational dialogs (turn-based workload).
- Liam: isolated tokenizer edge-case causing eval variance on code prompts. Patch submitted in PR #418 to tokenizer normalization — blocked on CI.
- Priya: started controlled A/B for model A vs model A-quant-4bit on internal eval harness. Preliminary human eval shows slight formatting artifacts (list numbering) more often in quantized variant.
- Marco: infra tuned autoscaler policy for dedicated nodes to prefer lower-latency pools during canary rollout window.

3) Experiment summary
- Exp Q-221: hybrid 4/8-bit kernels + kv-prefetch
  - Config: quant-profile = hybrid-v2, microbatch = 4, kv-prefetch = true, sequence = 8192
  - Metrics: throughput +10% (p95), latency +1% (median), cost/token -6% on our cost model
  - Quality: eval-suite-small (127 prompts) delta: avg ppl +0.9, CodeEval subset +1.5 ppl
  - Notes: regression concentrated on constructs with long-range dependencies (code + math). Hypothesis: int4 weight packing reduces effective dynamic range for a subset of attention heads.

- Exp Q-224: symmetric-int4 reorder test
  - Config: reorder=pack-rows vs pack-blocks
  - Result: pack-blocks restored some quality on code prompts but reduced throughput by 4%.
  - Decision: keep pack-blocks for now for code-heavy customers; add routing policy to use pack-rows for chat-heavy traffic.

4) Failures / oddities
- Stochastic eval variance: some runs differ by >2 ppl across runs (same seed). Suspect nondeterminism from microbatching + async cache eviction in runtime. Action: force deterministic mem alloc for next run.
- Tokenization mismatch: tokenizer patch fixes 2/3 of failing cases, but one class of escaped unicode sequences still inconsistent between python and Rust tokenizer implementations. Open issue filed.

5) Onboarding checklist status (model A)
- Model download + integrity: done
- Conversion to opt format + quant profiles generated: done (profiles hybrid-v2, int4-symmetric)
- Perf smoke: passes latency SLO (p95 < 350ms) on dedicated pool at scale=50
- Cost smoke: FAIL — high cost due to suboptimal batching and small effective batch sizes observed in prod-like harness
- Eval smoke: slight formatting regressions on docs and code tasks
- Blocks: need batching config change (try microbatch=2 + dynamic_batcher window=16ms), and decide pack-blocks vs pack-rows routing.

6) Action items (owners)
- Aisha: run deterministic microbatch-only reruns (Exp Q-221 deterministic) and upload traces by Fri EOD (JIRA: ML-7823).
- Liam: follow up on tokenizer PR #418, add Rust interop test for escaped unicode sequences; target Thu.
- Priya: expand eval suite with extra code-formatting prompts (50 new items from customer bug reports), run AB test Monday.
- Marco: add runtime flag to toggle pack-blocks per model route; prototype in staging and link to canary policy by next week.
- SRE: (CC) look into autoscaler warmup to avoid transient tiny batch windows that increase cost.

7) Open design questions
- Do we standardize on pack-blocks for all 4-bit profiles given quality wins, or prefer pack-rows and route per-traffic-shape? Tradeoffs: latency/throughput vs quality for specific tasks.
- How aggressive should default microbatch windows be? Current 16ms window gives better quality for throughput but increases 95th latency for single-turn chat by ~10ms.
- Do we add a quantization-caveat tag to model catalog entries (e.g., "avoid-for-code") until we improve int4 behavior? This would help customers avoid surprises but increases catalog complexity.

8) Quick notes from experiments logs
- flame_20280328_Aisha_expQ221.tar.gz attached to PR artifact
- CI failing on PR #418 due to linter on tokenizer; ignoring for now until tests pass
- Customer sample (acct: beta-enc-03) shows similar formatting errors — reached out to SE for examples.

9) Calendar / syncs
- Next deep-dive: Wed 2028-04-04 10:30am PT — bring deterministic run results and routing experiment plan.
- Canaries: aiming to start pack-blocks canary for model A on dedicated-2 cluster next Tue.

10) Misc / notes to self
- Remember to log microbatch/window config into rollout manifest (so we can revert easily).
- Add a short on-call note for SRE about temporary CPU spikes during quant conversion step.
- Phone note: ask Research about trying per-head scaling factors for int4 as an interim fix.

END — rough log. Will tidy into a formal brief if experiments confirm hypotheses.
